transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-07-15 16:32 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (VP Infra, Frostline), Samir Patel (Security), Lena Ortiz (Cloud Networking), Evan Ross (SRE)

Summary:
High-level intake on Frostline's requirements for a Private deployment of Redwood (Private/VPC). Primary concerns: region residency constraints (EU/US boundaries), private connectivity options (AWS PrivateLink vs VPC peering vs Transit Gateway), IP/CIDR overlap across multiple accounts, egress control & audit logging, key management (customer KMS/HSM), and SSO/SCIM for operator access. They want a pilot in two regions with a deterministic latency SLO and proof of no public internet egress for model-serving traffic.

Topics discussed:
- Current infra and account topology
- Preferred connectivity (Direct Connect/PrivateLink/peering)
- IP/CIDR planning and overlap avoidance
- DNS and split-horizon resolution for private endpoints
- Egress & outbound access controls + egress logging
- KMS integration and in-transit encryption
- Regional compliance (data residency) constraints
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Action items quick recap (also in metadata) followed by long transcript.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Rivera: All right everyone thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, um, I have Priya from our infra team. Priya say hi?
[00:08] Priya Menon: Hi folks, Priya here. I'll be the technical lead for the Private deployment.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Maya from Frostline, thanks Alex. We have Samir, Lena and Evan on too.
[00:17] Samir Patel: Quick heads up — security will be pretty strict here, SOC2 plus internal E2E encryption checks.
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: And I'm focused on the network: CIDR, peering, DNS.

[00:30] Alex Rivera: Great. High level, you're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, right? Can you walk us through the must-haves for Private?
[00:38] Maya Chen: Yes. Two must-haves: data residency — model inputs and logs for EU tenants must remain in eu-west-1, and no public internet egress from inference plane. Second — ability to use our KMS/HSM for key wrapping, not Redwood-managed keys.
[00:52] Priya Menon: Understood. For the no-public-egress, are you thinking full on VPC-only with PrivateLink endpoints, or would Transit Gateway peering be acceptable?
[01:01] Lena Ortiz: Prefer PrivateLink where possible, but we have a lot of accounts and some on-prem networks that go over Direct Connect into AWS. So TGW could simplify but we need to check inter-region routing and costs.
[01:12] Evan Ross: Also we can't change our core CIDR ranges easily — some are /16s, others /18. Overlaps are a likely showstopper for peering.

[01:22] Alex Rivera: Right, IP overlap kills standard VPC peering. We typically recommend PrivateLink for cross-account, avoids CIDR overlap; or we can do Transit Gateway with route tables and centralised NAT, but TGW requires non-overlapping too if you want direct peering? (inaudible)
[01:38] Priya Menon: Small correction — TGW still has constraints; TGW spokes can have overlapping space only if you use centralized NAT and proxying, but that's brittle. For model-serving traffic we usually propose Private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) or Private Service Connect equivalent in GCP. That lifts the CIDR overlap issue and gives you an NLB in our VPC with interface endpoints in your accounts.

[01:56] Samir Patel: How do we do egress e2e verification then — we need to show there's no path to public internet and capture flows for audit.
[02:03] Priya Menon: You can flow logs from our NLB and from your VPC endpoints; also VPC flow logs + Transit Gateway flow logs if used. We'll also enable audit logging in the control plane; Redwood can push logs to your S3 or to your account via cross-account role.

[02:18] Lena Ortiz: DNS — if we have interface endpoints across accounts, how does split-horizon DNS look? We're using private hosted zones, but some services need internal FQDN mapping to internal IP.
[02:26] Priya Menon: Good question. For AWS we recommend creating a private hosted zone in your route53 and then creating alias records that resolve to the VPC endpoint. Alternatively, we can support inbound DNS override through Route 53 Resolver rules; we sometimes provide a small BIND for on-prem but that gets messy.

[02:40] Alex Rivera: Also important -- latency SLOs. Maya, what are you targeting?
[02:44] Maya Chen: For inference median under 120ms and p95 under 300ms for our most common prompt sizes. If Private routing adds more than 50ms we'd need to consider Dedicated region placement.

[02:55] Priya Menon: We'll share our region latency matrix and typical model footprints; PrivateLink generally adds a few ms only but depends on whether traffic crosses Direct Connect or goes through TGW. We'll run a pilot in eu-west-1 + us-west-2 to measure.

[03:08] Evan Ross: For Private pilot, who will own the endpoints — do you create the NLB in Redwood account or in our account?
[03:13] Priya Menon: Our standard pattern is we run the model-serving NLB in Redwood's private VPC and you create interface endpoints in your accounts that connect to it. That minimizes ops on your side. We can also do a partner model where the NLB is in your account but that needs more setup and is less common.

[03:26] Samir Patel: For keys: KMS integration — do you support key wrapping with customer-managed keys? We need HSM-backed keys.
[03:33] Priya Menon: Yes, we support CMEK: Customer-managed keys via cross-account grants. For HSM we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM using envelope encryption; we'll need a key policy and a cross-account role for KMS decrypt. We'll document the exact IAM grant.

[03:46] Lena Ortiz: Any nuance for Azure or GCP? We have some workloads on GCP.
[03:50] Priya Menon: For GCP we recommend Private Service Connect; similar idea. For Azure it's Private Endpoint + Private Link Service. The concepts map but the names differ. We'll include a vendor matrix in the follow-up doc.

[04:02] Alex Rivera: On region restrictions: you said eu-west-1 only for EU tenants. Does that also apply to KV cache / model weights storage?
[04:09] Maya Chen: Everything inferences touch — cache, logs, traces — must stay in eu-west-1 for EU customers. We can allow meta telemetry to move, but not logs or raw prompts.

[04:18] Priya Menon: We can pin model-serving clusters to region and ensure KV cache locality. That also helps with latency. We'll need to coordinate where keys live and where audit logs get stored.

[04:28] Evan Ross: What's the onboarding window and how long is a typical pilot?
[04:31] Alex Rivera: From start of engineering scoping to pilot usually 4-8 weeks depending on CIDR mapping and approvals. Some customers have taken longer due to legal.

[04:38] Samir Patel: About SSO — we need SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning for operator accounts and RBAC scoped to projects.
[04:45] Priya Menon: Redwood supports SAML + SCIM and can integrate with Okta/AzureAD. RBAC is configurable per workspace and per model route; we'll share the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints in the security pack.

[04:56] Lena Ortiz: MTU, fragmentation — we move some large payloads, can you confirm max MTU support? We've had issues with encapsulation over Direct Connect.
[05:04] Priya Menon: Sorry small glitch — priya: we generally assume standard 1500 MTU. If you have jumbo frames on your DC we'll need to test during the pilot; the endpoint interface does not change MTU but encapsulation over VPN can. We'll note that as an item for Evan to test.

[05:18] Alex Rivera: Are you planning to host model weights in your account or ours?
[05:22] Maya Chen: We'd like weights to stay with Redwood on your private compute, but with strict access controls — we want an SLA that says weights for EU tenants are never replicated outside eu-west-1.

[05:31] Priya Menon: We can do that, we support region pinning and model-version pinning. We'll document guardrails and can add a contractual clause for region residency.

[05:38] Samir Patel: Audit trail — we need proof of access to keys and who invoked model calls. How granular are logs?
[05:44] Priya Menon: We capture token-level metadata, request IDs, timestamps, and can stream logs to your account. Full prompt text can be redacted or routed to your S3. For deeper forensic needs we can provide read-only views via cross-account role.

[05:55] Evan Ross: Network firewall — do you need outbound NAT? We want to block any outbound to the internet entirely.
[06:00] Priya Menon: Our PrivateLink pattern avoids outbound internet for inference calls; management/control plane calls (initial provisioning) sometimes require connectivity to our control plane — for fully airgapped we offer an on-prem package but for VPC Private deployments we can tunnel control plane traffic via your NAT or a dedicated management link. We'll document options.

[06:16] Lena Ortiz: Licensing and pricing question — is Private priced as a multiplier on Dedicated?
[06:20] Alex Rivera: Typically Private is quoted as a combination of dedicated capacity plus a deployment/region fee because of private networking and additional SLA/ops. I'll send a delta sheet.

[06:27] Samir Patel: Any customer references with similar constraints?
[06:30] Alex Rivera: We have a few — I'll share two references in regulated industries who did PrivateLink-based deployments with KMS.

[06:36] Maya Chen: Great. For next steps I'd like a CIDR mapping call and then a separate security deep dive with Samir.

[06:43] Priya Menon: Works for us. We'll propose times. Also we'll draft a pilot runbook with success criteria: latency targets, security validations (no public egress), and audit log delivery.

[06:55] Alex Rivera: Quick recap: Redwood to share Private deployment design doc + region matrix + pricing delta; Priya to run CIDR workshop; Frostline to share VPC list and SAML details; schedule security deep dive. Anything else?
[07:07] Maya Chen: That's it. Thanks.
[07:10] Alex Rivera: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the attachments and a calendar invite for the CIDR workshop.

End of recorded transcript.

Notes on transcription noise: occasional label swap around 05:04 where timestamp lacked bracket. Some words transcribed phonetically (PrivateLink sometimes as 'private link', TGW annotated as 'T G W' then 'transit gateway'), minor filler words and interruptions remain.
